newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World ups Chinese 96/97 soya import estimates.
newsitem.headline: Oil World ups Chinese 96/97 soya import estimates.

text.p: Chinese soybean imports were forecast at 1.60 million tonnes in 1996/97 (Oct/Sept) and soymeal at 2.70 million, up from previous forecasts of 1.50 million and 2.65 million, Oil World newsletter said.
China's soybean imports in 95/96 were 790,000 tonnes with soymeal at 1.64 million, according to Oil World.
It said domestic production had fallen because more land was devoted to grains and flood damage had reduced yields, but domestic demand was expanding and stocks were falling.
A shortfall in domestic seed oil supply would also bring more imports of finished oils and fats products which would supplement higher domestic animal fats output.

Chinese imports of 17 oils and fats in the 96/97 season were put at 4.18 million tonnes, 946,000 more than in 95/96. Of that, soy oil accounted for 1.58 million tonnes (1.45 million 95/96) and palm oil for 1.78 million (1.09). --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
